claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are near the top at keeping shots away. We think the Avalanche still get theirs.
claims.call: The Avalanche’s shot volume score is above 100, the league average, against the Devils.

claims.head: Strength against strength
claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.

claims.head: The Avalanche like Schwartz’s line against Mantha’s
claims.call: The Avalanche’s L3 (Schwartz, Svechkov and Hughes) spends at least 41% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Avalanche keep sending Schwartz’s line (Schwartz, Svechkov and Hughes) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jared Bednar keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Devils’ third line is Mantha, Rodrigues and Mercer.
claims.nums: At home: 41% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 31% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Colorado home games this season · 6 games, 38 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Colorado’s L3 (Schwartz, Svechkov and Hughes) at home: 41% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, Colorado home games this season, 6 games, 38 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 31% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: Tired legs for the Devils
claims.body: The Devils played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Avalanche to control more of the play than they usually do.
claims.call: The Avalanche get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.

COL.head: A genuine toss-up
COL.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Colorado has home-ice advantage. For the Avalanche, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.

NJD.head: Nothing to separate these two
NJD.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Colorado has home-ice advantage. For the Devils, the difference could be piling up shots.

story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Devils won the first meeting this season, 4-3 in New Jersey. The Avalanche are 6-4-1. The Devils have won two in a row.

It’s strength against strength: the Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are near the top at keeping shots away. At home, Jared Bednar likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ third line.

lean.COL: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Colorado has home-ice advantage. For the Avalanche, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.
lean.NJD: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Colorado has home-ice advantage. For the Devils, the difference could be piling up shots.
